I would keep the usual Quzhou pattern and run the same land in a winter wheat to summer maize rotation. In my county that is the safest way for me to hold grain output, use my machinery efficiently, and avoid gambling on a crop I know less well. I would not split much land into cotton, vegetables, or peanuts, because that adds market risk, more labor at key moments, and more management complexity than I want. With my background and what I trust, I would stay with the grain system I understand best.

I need one practical assumption to make this concrete, so I will assume I am farming 20 mu of ordinary irrigated land. On those 20 mu, I would finish the winter wheat already in the ground, then turn the same 20 mu into summer maize right after harvest. I would use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed, because that is the balance I would choose between cost, yield, and reliability. I would keep fertilizer moderate rather than chase extreme yield, use rotary tillage between crops for speed, irrigate a few key times instead of too often, and spray only when disease, weeds, or insects justify it. My goal would be stable grain, controlled cash cost, and low risk through the whole year.
